The Emergence of Dark Nebula Lynds 1251 Explanation: If you stare into space for a long time, what might you see? At first, you might only see the usual brightest stars , but if your eyes (or camera) could continue to collect light , you would see increasingly more. In the direction of the featured image , after only a few minutes, you would begin to notice some regions without stars . As your staring continued, the dark region would become better defined, and after a full 20 hours, you would notice a strange dark structure . To celebrate, you use digital processing to brighten the image and enhance the colors. At the end, you might have an excellent image of Lynds 1251 (LDN 1251), a star -forming region laced with opaque brown-appearing interstellar dust. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate . What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image — and many similar images — is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. Voyager’s Neptune Explanation: Cruising through the outer solar system, the Voyager 2 spacecraft made its closest approach to Neptune on August 25, 1989, the only spacecraft to visit the most distant ice giant planet . Based on the images recorded during its close encounter and in the following days, this inspired composited scene covers the dim outer planet, largest moon Triton , and faint system of rings. From just beyond Neptune’s orbit, the interplanetary perspective looks back toward the Sun, capturing the planet and Triton as thin sunlit crescents . Cirrus clouds and a dark band circle Neptune’s south polar region, with a cloudy vortex above the pole itself . title: Your Android device could soon become your PC’s second screen via Link to Windows
summary: Need extra screen space? Your Android tablet or phone could soon become your second PC monitor.
body: Credit: Tushar Mehta / Android Authority TL;DR Strings of code in the Link to Windows app reveal a second screen experience called “Extend display.” This feature would turn your Android phone or tablet into a second screen for your PC. The experience will stop if your PC locks, the connection is lost, or if the phone’s display receiver fails. When you’ve grown accustomed to a dual-screen setup, it’s hard to go back to using a single screen. If you don’t have an extra monitor handy, you could turn your old tablet into a second screen with spacedesk . Samsung also offers a Second Screen feature on select Galaxy tablets. However, if you want a more convenient option than these, Microsoft is building a solution. The folks over at Windows Latest have spotted new strings of code in the Link to Windows app. These strings of code reference a feature called “Extend display.” Aptly named, this feature would allow you to extend your PC’s screen to your Android phone or tablet.

V-G-R Explanation: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory are read V-G-R. That’s a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft currently in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away. How long did it take the message to reach humanity’s most distant interstellar spacecraft ? Traveling at the speed of light, the answer is one day . In fact, the Voyager 1 spacecraft was confirmed to reach its one light-day distance milestone on November 18, at 10:16:07 UTC, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977.
